analysis: Integration review of the SSD cache single-copy read change. The only production change is SSDBlockStore.readExactly (patch hunks @@ -481 and @@ -494). It removes the up-front out.reserveCapacity(count). When the first non-empty read returns exactly `count` bytes with startIndex == 0, it now returns that buffer uncopied; otherwise it reserves capacity and appends as before. The beforeRead(count) charge, the per-iteration beforeRead(0) charge, the truncation throw on nil chunk before `count` bytes, and the loop bound are unchanged. A short read still takes the assemble path, so no partial or unauthenticated data is returned from this function. The returned bytes are raw file fields and ciphertext chunks. AES-256-GCM chunk and AAD authentication, DEK unwrap, HMAC lookup tags (K_lookup), the TTL, the disk budget and the no-follow I/O are untouched. This matches the T-041 mitigations (a)-(e) with no widening of the at-rest exposure. Deferring reserveCapacity until after a successful non-empty read is slightly beneficial: a header that claims a large length but is truncated no longer causes an up-front allocation. The per-field caps (maxHeaderFieldBytes, per unit 2's reading of lines ~455/461) were not directly visible in the replayed patch. Unit 2 reports them as unchanged; I rely on that but did not verify them myself. The startIndex == 0 guard preserves zero-based indexing for callers. The added test readExactlyAssemblesShortReads (SSDBlockStreamingTests.swift, head lines 259-283) pins the charge sequences ([64,0] and [64,0,0]) and the zero start index, and it writes only to a temp fixture. The docs and changelog (docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md line 65, changelog.d/ssd-read-single-copy.md) accurately describe the behavior and add no new claims. No new attack surface or threat-model gap was identified. Residual unverified items: the readExactly callers (SSDBlockChunkCursor and others) and the chunk-read primitive are outside the supplied evidence. They are assumed to treat the result as an independent Data and not rely on aliasing or on a larger shared backing buffer. I also did not confirm that the retry raw-byte budget is still charged before allocation. Both are expected to hold from the unchanged beforeRead call, which was visible.
